page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server built on the ARMv9 architecture. The system is equipped with AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors offering 192 physical cores running at 2.7 GHz, delivering 192 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core and no hyperthreading overhead. It incorporates 768 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is configured with 11,400 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 50 Gbps. The server operates as a bare-metal system without hypervisor intervention and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational and memory subsystem bandwidth. The system achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 298,073.2 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 21,219.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 895.56 GB/s, while write bandwidth measures 426.24 GB/s. Software compilation with Clang scores 86,345.0, reflecting strong parallel execution across all 192 physical cores. Application benchmarks confirm top-tier throughput in key-value workloads, registering 391.52 million Redis SET operations per second and 150.44 GB/s in static web serving.

Performance tradeoffs correspond directly to the arm64 architecture and thread topology. While multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth are extensive, single-core metrics fall within the middle 50%, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,663.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,648.69. Similarly, LLM inference text generation speeds are weak due to the absence of dedicated matrix acceleration hardware, although prompt processing remains competitive through high core density. Cost efficiency is high for workloads that maximize thread utilization and local I/O, as the bundled 11.4 TB NVMe array removes the need for separate high-IOPS network storage attachments.

The m8gd.metal-48xl is best suited for large-scale distributed databases, high-throughput in-memory caching systems such as Redis, intensive parallel compilation farms, and containerized microservice clusters that require low-latency access to extensive local NVMe storage and balanced core-to-memory density.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server driven by 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 768 GB of DDR5 system memory alongside 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. With a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, the server yields top-tier multi-threaded processing throughput, evidenced by strong multi-core Geekbench scores, rapid Clang compilation times, and over 391 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 895.56 GB/s for large uncached reads, supporting data-intensive services. While single-thread performance and GPU-free generative token production remain modest, the combination of dedicated bare-metal execution and dense local storage delivers high efficiency for scaled enterprise workloads. It is well suited for distributed NoSQL databases, in-memory key-value caches, parallel software build clusters, and high-concurrency microservice architectures.
